Omit 'claim' to get the full list; pass the request in 'claim' (e.g. 'print a document') to check that one thing. description: Creates and manages the user's SCHEDULED TASKS: a reminder, one Era tool call, or a CHAIN of tool calls run in order, at a time or on a repeat ('schedule task backup at 18:00', 'run X every day/week/month', 'every weekday at 9 run my morning routine'). Use `steps` for a routine that is several commands — ONE task, not one task per command. Tasks run autonomously and report back. When due, a risky action parks for the user's approval unless they waived confirmation for that task; a chain is gated, approved and reported as a single unit. A task may carry a `condition` to poll a read-only check and act (or stop) only when it is met ('check every 5 minutes until the download finishes, then tell me'). Actions: create | list | status | steps | update | pause | resume | cancel | run_now | approve | skip | waive_confirmation | require_confirmation | results | pending.

action.description: create | list | status | steps | update | pause | resume | cancel | run_now | approve | skip | waive_confirmation | require_confirmation | results | pending

catch_up_until.description: HH:MM, recurring daily/weekday times only: if Era was not running at the scheduled time, run it ONCE when Era launches, as long as it is before this time that day (later launches report it as missed). Use when the user says e.g. 'when I launch you in the morning'. 'off' clears it.

condition.description: Conditional task ('until'/'if'): a JSON object gating the action on a READ-ONLY check run each time it is due. Use on a REPEAT (every N minutes/etc.) to poll until something happens. Shape: {"check": {"tool": "file_controller", "args": {"action": "last_download"}}, "operator": "contains", "value": "complete", "on_met": "stop"}. operator: truthy (check succeeded) | falsy | contains | not_contains | equals | changed; value is the text compared for contains/not_contains/equals. on_met: stop (retire the task once met — 'keep checking UNTIL X') | continue (default; keep the schedule, act each time the check holds — 'each day IF X'). The action/reminder/steps run only when the check is met; when it is not, the task waits for the next time silently. 'off' clears it. The check must be a read-only action.

include_finished.description: list: include one-shot tasks that already ran

name.description: Short name for a NEW task (create)

notify.description: all (default) | failures | silent — which run results to announce; approval requests are always announced

on_error.description: chain only: stop (default — a failed step is reported and the remaining steps do NOT run) | continue (the failed step is reported before the rest run). Set continue only if the user asked for it.

steps.description: CHAIN (use instead of tool/tool_args): JSON array of the tool calls to run IN ORDER under this ONE task, e.g. [{"tool": "weather_report", "args": {"city": "Tunis"}}, {"tool": "gmail_control", "args": {"action": "important"}}, {"tool": "spotify_control", "args": {"action": "search", "value": "calm music"}}]. Each entry is exactly the call you would make if asked to do that step now; an optional 'label' names the step. 2 to 8 steps. Use whenever the user's routine is several commands under one schedule — never split it into separate tasks. A step may carry a "run_if" (same shape as `condition`, minus on_met) to run that ONE step only when a read-only check is met, e.g. {"tool": "spotify_control", "args": {...}, "run_if": {"check": {"tool": "computer_control", "args": {"action": "running_apps"}}, "operator": "not_contains", "value": "zoom"}}; a step whose run_if is not met is skipped and the chain goes on.

task.description: Existing task's name or id (all actions except create/list)

tool.description: The Era tool the task calls when it runs, e.g. weather_report

tool_args.description: JSON object of that tool's arguments, e.g. {"city": "Montreal"}

waive_confirmation.description: true ONLY when the user explicitly said to run it without asking (create)

when.description: The user's time phrase, copied as said: 'at 14:30', 'tomorrow at 9', 'in 20 minutes', 'every day at 8', 'every monday at 10', 'every 2 hours', 'every month on the 1st at 9', 'cron: 0 9 * * mon-fri'

description: Controls the COMPUTER ITSELF: volume, brightness, window management, keyboard shortcuts, typing text on screen, closing apps, fullscreen, dark mode, WiFi, Bluetooth, scrolling, tab management, zoom, screenshots, lock screen, refresh/reload page, AND Spotify playback execution. This is ALSO the tool that shuts down or restarts the MACHINE: 'shut down the computer/PC/laptop' -> action='shutdown'; 'restart the computer/reboot' -> action='restart'; 'cancel the shutdown' -> action='cancel_shutdown'. Never use shutdown_era for those — shutdown_era only closes Era herself and leaves the computer running. Use computer_settings for ANY single computer control command.

Options include: volume_up, volume_down, mute, toggle_mute, dark_mode, screenshot, lock_screen, close_app, minimize, maximize, refresh_page, shutdown (powers the MACHINE off), restart (reboots the MACHINE), cancel_shutdown (aborts a shutdown/restart still counting down), spotify_play, spotify_pause, spotify_next, spotify_previous, spotify_like, spotify_dislike, spotify_search, spotify_liked_songs, spotify_new_releases, spotify_made_for_you, spotify_volume_up, spotify_volume_down. Bluetooth: bluetooth_on / bluetooth_off switch the RADIO itself (prefer these over toggle_bluetooth whenever the user names a direction, so 'turn Bluetooth on' can never switch it off), bluetooth_status reports whether it is on, bluetooth_settings opens the Windows Bluetooth page. To connect or disconnect a PAIRED DEVICE (a speaker, headphones, earbuds — 'connect to my Marley speaker', 'disconnect the JBL'), use action='connect_device' or action='disconnect_device' and put the device's name in value. Never turn the whole radio off just to drop one device. shutdown and restart require the user's confirmation: Era will return ConfirmationRequired with a confirmation_id — ask the user out loud, and only when they agree, call again with confirmed=true and that confirmation_id.

description: Audio DEVICES: list every speaker/headphone/microphone with its live level, switch the default output or input, and control the volume or mute of ONE NAMED device (any output or any microphone). ROUTING RULE: a general volume command with no device named ('volume up', 'mute', 'set volume to 50') is NOT for this tool - use computer_settings, which drives the SYSTEM volume. Use audio_control only when the user names a device ('turn the headset mic down', 'mute my microphone', 'set the speakers to 30', 'switch output to the glasses', 'what audio devices do I have'). ALSO owns where YOUR OWN SPOKEN VOICE plays (set_voice_output) and the battery level of connected audio devices (battery).

action.description: list_devices (all devices + live volume/mute + which is default) | set_default (make `device` the default output or input - this moves MEDIA: Spotify, YouTube, everything. It does NOT move my voice) | set_voice_output (play MY OWN SPOKEN VOICE on `device` - 'speak on my glasses', 'switch your voice to the computer', 'talk through the speakers'. Persistent, instant, and it leaves media routing alone) | clear_voice_output (stop pinning my voice; back to the automatic route) | voice_output (where does my voice play right now?) | battery (battery level of `device`, or of every audio device that reports one - 'how much battery do my glasses have') | device_status | device_volume_set (value 0-100) | device_volume_up | device_volume_down | device_mute | device_unmute | device_toggle_mute | glass_volume_up | glass_volume_down | glass_volume_set (value 0-100) | glass_mute | glass_unmute | glass_volume (the Star Glasses ONLY - use these for 'glasses volume up', 'turn the glasses down', 'set the glasses to 40'; they hit the glasses even with no `device` given) | app_preference (does Windows pin MY OWN audio to one device regardless of the system default?) | clear_app_preference (drop that pin - only when the user asks, it changes a Windows setting). Prefer device_mute / device_unmute over device_toggle_mute unless the user literally said 'toggle'. Never confuse set_default (media) with set_voice_output (my voice) - they are different requests.

device.description: The device the user NAMED: its name (or part of it), 'speakers', 'headset', 'microphone', or 'glasses'. Never guess or invent one - if unsure, call list_devices first. If several devices match, the tool returns the candidates: ask the user which.

description: Save an important personal fact about the user to long-term memory. YOU decide when to call it — the user does NOT have to say 'remember this'. Call it silently, without asking permission, whenever the user reveals something durable in passing: name, age, city, job, preferences and things they love or hate, hobbies, relationships, projects, plans, and DATES that matter to them (birthdays, deadlines, trips, appointments). 'I love this film' or 'my flight is on the 12th' is enough — save it. Do NOT call for: weather, reminders, searches, one-time commands, or transient state. Do NOT save anything you merely READ on screen, in a web page or a document — only what the USER told you. Do NOT announce that you are saving — just call it silently. Build the value out of the user's OWN WORDS: keep names, titles and places exactly as they said them, and never paraphrase or translate a fact into words they did not use.
